title: Investigating the role of G-quadruplex-associated duplex stem loops in Trabectedin’s mechanism of action
task: Elucidate Trabectedin's mechanism of action through its interaction with G-quadruplex-duplex stem-loop architectures
key_results: Trabectedin stabilizes G4–duplex composites via covalent bonding to guanine in hairpin loops; LC-MS affinity assays show duplex DNA preference retained; cellular treatment increases G4 frequency
comments: Proposes novel 'search and lock' mechanism balancing Trabectedin's duplex preference with G4-stem-loop engagement; LC-MS data supports context-dependent recognition but duplex dominance remains primary.

model_io.model: Trabectedin–DNA interaction assays

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trabectedin interacts preferentially with G4-associated duplex stem loops due to EWS–G4 biology in Ewing sarcoma
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed: Trabectedin engages G4–duplex composites but retains duplex DNA preference; mechanism refined to context-dependent recognition

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trabectedin's superior potency vs. Saframycin A relates to enhanced G4-stem-loop reactivity
hypotheses.result: Supported by proposed 'search and lock' mechanism and observed G4 frequency modulation in cells

title: Mapping the thymus in the viscoelastic landscape of biological tissues
task: Characterize thymic tissue viscoelastic properties and extracellular matrix architecture across multiple scales
key_results: Thymus identified as compliant, highly dissipative viscoelastic organ; quantified relaxation times, elastic moduli (instantaneous and equilibrium), and storage/loss moduli under varied loading conditions
comments: First comprehensive multiscale mechanical dataset for thymus tissue; provides benchmark values for engineering applications but limited to bovine model generalization.

model_io.model: Bovine thymic tissue mechanical testing

hypotheses.hypothesis: Thymic mechanical properties correlate with 3D architecture and support organ function
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: viscoelastic behavior quantified and linked to fibrillar architecture

title: UNC5B regulates epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through a SRC-ZEB1 signaling axis to facilitate pancreatic cancer metastasis
task: Characterize UNC5B-driven epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition via SRC-ZEB1 axis in pancreatic cancer metastasis
key_results: UNC5B loss abolishes metastatic spread, reduces proliferation, increases intratumoral necrosis in KPCU and orthotopic models; UNC5B specifically drives EMT via SRC-ZEB1 without altering SNAIL/TWIST1; targeted protein degradation modulates EMT and invasion; acute UNC5B depletion reduces EMT scores and ZEB1/SRC levels
comments: Strong in vivo validation using genetically engineered models and demonstration of ZEB1-specific regulation (independent of other EMT factors) is notable; potential therapeutic window via protein degrader approach is promising.

model_io.model: KPCU and orthotopic PDAC models; PDAC cell lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: UNC5B is essential for PDAC metastasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: UNC5B loss completely abolishes metastatic dissemination

hypotheses.hypothesis: UNC5B drives EMT specifically via ZEB1, not other EMT TFs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ZEB1 modulation observed; SNAIL and TWIST1 unchanged

title: Chondroitin sulfate shapes the unfolded protein response in osteosarcoma to sustain cancer cell survival during ER stress
task: Define role of chondroitin sulfate in UPR-mediated osteosarcoma survival
key_results: CS 4-O-sulfation enables GRP78 upregulation under ER stress; CS-deficient cells undergo apoptosis upon acute ER stress; oncofetal CS protects dissociated osteosarcoma cells from anoikis during pulmonary colonization
comments: Identifies an unexpected extracellular glycan as essential for canonical UPR signaling, though the precise molecular mechanism linking CS to GRP78 expression remains unelucidated.

model_io.model: osteosarcoma cells (2D and in vivo metastasis)

hypotheses.hypothesis: CS 4-O-sulfation is required for robust UPR adaptation in osteosarcoma
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CS-deficient cells fail to induce GRP78 and are hypersensitive to ER stress

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oncofetal CS protects metastatic osteosarcoma from anoikis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in pulmonary colonization mouse model

title: The anti-tumour activity of TNF in melanoma is determined by cFLIP
task: Establish cFLIP as critical determinant of TNF-mediated melanoma control in immune-competent context
key_results: cFLIP expression determines melanoma susceptibility to TNF; cFlipKO/KO melanoma cells failed to grow in wild-type mice but formed tumors in TNF-deficient mice; TNF-induced cytotoxicity independent of cIAP/RIPK1 inhibition; cFLIP targeting could enhance endogenous immune surveillance and TNF-based immunotherapies
comments: Elegant genetic approach elegantly dissects the cFLIP-dependent vs. cIAP/RIPK1-dependent TNF signaling pathways, challenging prior therapeutic paradigms and providing strong preclinical rationale for cFLIP-targeting strategies.

model_io.model: B16F10 melanoma syngeneic model (wild-type and TNF-deficient mice)

hypotheses.hypothesis: cFLIP expression protects melanoma from TNF-induced death
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: cFlipKO/KO cells killed by TNF in vivo

hypotheses.hypothesis: TNF-mediated melanoma control depends on cFLIP, not cIAPs/RIPK1
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: cIAP/RIPK1 ablation did not phenocopy cFLIP loss

title: Epigenetics drives oocyte aging: from mechanisms to interventions
task: Synthesize epigenetic mechanisms driving oocyte aging and identify interventions
key_results: DNA methylation disruption, histone modifications, RNA modifications, and ncRNA dysregulation impair meiosis and developmental competence; NAD+ precursors and sirtuin activation offer mechanistic opportunities
comments: Comprehensive review connecting epigenetic dysregulation to age-related fertility decline, but translational application remains limited by complexity and interplay of multiple pathways.

model_io.model: aged oocytes (mouse and human)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Epigenetic dysregulation is the primary driver of oocyte aging
hypotheses.result: Supported: multiple epigenetic modifications correlate with reduced developmental competence

hypotheses.hypothesis: NAD+ precursors and sirtuin activation improve aged oocyte quality
hypotheses.result: Supported in preclinical models, but translational outcomes not yet established

title: Aging of the neural stem cell niche: integration of local and muscle-derived systemic signals in preclinical and translational contexts
task: Characterize integration of local and systemic signals in neural stem cell aging
key_results: Muscle-derived myokines and metabolites improve NSC niche function; exercise and parabiosis studies demonstrate reversibility of age-related NSC decline; local niche inflammation contributes to functional deterioration
comments: Emphasizes bidirectional communication between muscle and brain, offering therapeutic opportunities through exercise, though the specific mechanistic mediators require further delineation.

model_io.model: aged neural stem cells and niche cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Muscle-derived systemic signals can rejuvenate NSC niches in aging
hypotheses.result: Supported: parabiosis and myokine administration improve NSC function

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local niche inflammation is rate-limiting for age-related NSC decline
hypotheses.result: Partially supported; inflammation correlates with dysfunction but causal role requires further validation

title: Integrated computational and in vitro analysis reveals the toxic mechanisms of PFAS in female diminished ovarian reserve
task: Elucidate PFAS-induced diminished ovarian reserve mechanisms via integrated computational and in vitro analysis
key_results: PFAS induces dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity and oxidative stress in KGN cells; activates apoptosis via BAX upregulation/Bcl-2 downregulation; suppresses GSTP1/PRDX5 expression; inhibits AMH/INHB synthesis; upregulates TGFBR1 pro-fibrotic signaling
comments: Strong multi-platform integration (network toxicology, machine learning, MD simulations) identifies comprehensive mechanistic framework, but validation in primary oocytes and in vivo models is needed.

model_io.model: KGN cells (granulosa cells); computational analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: PFAS perturbs cell proliferation, immune responses, and hormone signaling pathways
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: KEGG enrichment analysis identified these pathways as primary targets

hypotheses.hypothesis: PFAS induces apoptosis and oxidative stress in ovarian cells
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: dose-dependent BAX upregulation, Bcl-2 downregulation, and ROS elevation observed

title: Octa-arginine-modified calcium phosphate nanoparticles with amiloride enhance gene delivery and bone augmentation in rat calvaria
task: Enhance gene delivery to bone via amiloride-modified arginine-functionalized calcium phosphate nanoparticles
key_results: Amiloride increased transfection efficiency but showed cytotoxic effects; R8-modified CaP/amiloride with BMP-2 plasmid achieved highest local BMP-2 concentration and significantly enhanced bone formation in rat calvaria without severe inflammation; synergistic effect demonstrated despite smaller volume than recombinant BMP-2
comments: Mechanistic understanding of pH and calcium dynamics is valuable, but in vivo efficacy remains inferior to exogenous protein, limiting clinical translational potential.

model_io.model: MC3T3-E1 cells, rat BMSCs, rat calvaria defect

hypotheses.hypothesis: Amiloride enhances transfection by modulating intracellular pH and calcium dynamics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: amiloride reduced pH and increased Ca2+, promoting lysosomal aggregation toward nucleus

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combined R8/amiloride/BMP-2 enhances bone regeneration
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: significant enhancement in rat calvaria, though smaller volume than recombinant BMP-2

title: A novel CD69 binding ankyrin repeat protein (Ankyron®) enables detection of early activated and antigen-specific T cells in pigs
task: Develop ankyrin repeat protein tool for detecting porcine CD69 in T-cell activation studies
key_results: Ankyron EG40360 specifically binds porcine CD69; CD69 expressed as early as 4 h post-PMA/ionomycin stimulation; antigen-specific CD4/CD8 T cells detected post-vaccination via CD69/CD25 co-expression
comments: Practical immunology tool development filling a reagent gap in large animal models; validation is solid but application remains limited to CD69 detection without mechanistic insights into CD69 function.

model_io.model: porcine PBMCs and CD69-transfected HEK293T cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ankyron EG40360 specifically binds porcine CD69
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by flow cytometry and microscopy

hypotheses.hypothesis: CD69 marks early-activated and antigen-specific T cells in pigs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CD69 expression induced by PMA/ionomycin at 4 h and by vaccine restimulation

title: Quercetin ameliorates iron overload-induced liver injury via NRF2/GPX4 pathway
task: Demonstrate quercetin protection against iron overload-induced ferroptosis via NRF2/GPX4 pathway
key_results: Quercetin attenuated iron overload-induced liver injury, reduced ROS accumulation, improved iron metabolism; protective effects accompanied by NRF2/GPX4 pathway modulation in both in vivo (mouse) and in vitro (Hep G2) models
comments: Complementary in vivo and in vitro validation strengthens conclusions, but direct mechanistic proof of NRF2/GPX4 involvement (e.g., pathway inhibition) would enhance clarity.

model_io.model: iron overload mouse model; Hep G2 cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quercetin protects against iron overload-induced liver injury and ferroptosis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: significant reduction in ROS, improved liver function, enhanced ferroptosis resistance

hypotheses.hypothesis: NRF2/GPX4 pathway mediates quercetin's protective effects
hypotheses.result: Supported: pathway modulation correlates with protection, but direct causation not definitively proven

title: Bilirubin alleviates cigarette smoke extract-induced lung tissue inflammation and damage by suppressing macrophage pyroptosis
task: Establish bilirubin suppression of macrophage pyroptosis as mechanism protecting against CSE-induced lung inflammation
key_results: Bilirubin reduced CSE-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, suppressed macrophage pyroptosis-related proteins, alleviated inflammation, improved lung pathology and function; effects mediated via oxidative stress reduction and redox balance maintenance
comments: In vivo rat model is physiologically relevant, but the cell-type specificity of bilirubin's effects (macrophage-selective) and direct pyroptosis validation could be strengthened.

model_io.model: CSE-exposed Wistar rats; lung tissue

hypotheses.hypothesis: CSE induces macrophage pyroptosis-mediated lung inflammation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CSE elevated pyroptosis markers and inflammatory cytokines

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bilirubin suppresses CSE-induced pyroptosis by reducing mitochondrial dysfunction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: bilirubin improved ATP levels, reduced oxidative stress, and decreased pyroptosis marker expression

title: Spatially defined IGF1R-STMN1 axis delineates a metastatic cell state in osteosarcoma
task: Identify and validate IGF1R-STMN1 signaling axis driving osteosarcoma metastasis
key_results: STMN1+ OS cells enriched in metastatic samples show elevated migratory capacity; IGF1R-STMN1 co-targeting suppresses MAPK/AKT more potently than single-axis inhibition; combined disruption attenuates metastatic phenotypes in vitro and in vivo
comments: Well-integrated multi-omics approach identifies a spatially-defined therapeutic axis, though clinical validation in TARGET-OS cohort was limited; potential for combination therapy is promising.

model_io.model: osteosarcoma cells (scRNAseq, spatial transcriptomics, cell lines, xenografts)

hypotheses.hypothesis: STMN1+ OS cells represent a distinct metastatic subpopulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: STMN1+ cells enriched in metastatic samples with enhanced migration

hypotheses.hypothesis: IGF1R-STMN1 axis is co-dependent for metastatic phenotype
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: combined disruption more effective than single-axis targeting

title: CALIPERS: Cell cycle-aware live imaging for phenotyping experiments and regeneration studies
task: Enable cell-cycle-aware live-cell imaging across diverse phenotyping and regeneration assays
key_results: CALIPERS framework integrates spectrally redesigned FUCCI reporter with continuous cell-cycle inference; simultaneous imaging of actin/tubulin/calcium; cardiac organoids track cell-cycle exit and tissue compaction
comments: Novel integrated approach making cell-cycle state explicit in live imaging; diverse applications demonstrated (epithelial, iPSC, cardiac); technical implementation and reagent availability for widespread adoption unclear.

model_io.model: CALIPERS (cell-cycle inference + FUCCI reporter + flexible delivery)
inputs: human epithelial cells, iPSCs, cardiac organoids

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit cell-cycle state measurement improves phenotypic interpretation and triage of regenerative interventions across diverse live-cell assays
hypotheses.result: CALIPERS framework enables simultaneous multi-modal imaging and distinguishes productive proliferation from multinucleation in cardiac organoids

title: Deep-learning-enabled multi-omics analyses for prediction of future metastasis in cancer
task: Predict future metastasis and identify biomarkers in cancer
key_results: Superior sensitivity/specificity across 6 cancer types; HSP90AA1/AB1 validated in 420 patients; YY1 confirmed as metastasis driver via CRISPR and in vivo models
comments: Multi-omics integration is comprehensive but clinical translation requires prospective validation; HSP90 inhibition is mechanistically plausible but therapeutic applicability remains unproven.

model_io.model: EmitGCL deep-learning framework
inputs: multi-omics data across seven patient cohorts

hypotheses.hypothesis: HSP90 inhibition reduces breast cancer cell migration via targeted suppression
hypotheses.result: In vitro and multi-cohort validation (n=420) confirmed; HSP90AA1/AB1 identified as predictable biomarkers

hypotheses.hypothesis: YY1 transcription factor drives breast cancer metastasis
hypotheses.result: Validated via CRISPR-based assays, in silico analysis, and mouse lung colonization experiments

title: Machine learning image analysis predicts Parkinson disease genotype and mitochondrial lysosomal abnormalities in iPS neurons
task: Predict Parkinson disease genotype and mitochondrial-lysosomal dysfunction from iPSC neuron morphology
key_results: Cell morphomics distinguished PD from controls with AUC=0.87; genotype-specific organelle biases identified (mitochondrial in PRKN, balanced in SNCA, lysosomal in LRRK2); reproduced across two independent labs
comments: Elegant unsupervised morphological stratification; genotype-specific biases suggest distinct cellular pathologies, though functional consequences of organelle abnormalities require further investigation.

model_io.model: Cell morphomics framework (high-content imaging + supervised machine learning)
inputs: iPS-derived cortical neuron images from PD patients (3 genotypes: PRKN, SNCA, LRRK2) and controls (13 lines total)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Parkinson disease genotypes exhibit distinct mitochondrial and lysosomal morphological signatures at single-cell resolution
hypotheses.result: Genotype-specific organelle biases confirmed; features dominate in PRKN (mitochondrial), balanced in SNCA, lysosomal-dominant in LRRK2

title: Cross-gated feature interaction network for fetal abdominal circumference image segmentation
task: Fetal abdominal circumference segmentation in ultrasound images
key_results: CGFI-Net achieved Dice=0.9736, Accuracy=0.9929 on fetal dataset; cross-dataset validation on DDTI (Dice=0.8095); 3.21 GFLOPs, 6.10M parameters, 70 FPS inference speed
comments: Efficient multi-scale fusion architecture with strong boundary delineation; limited discussion of inter-operator variability and clinical-grade validation.

model_io.model: CGFI-Net (MobileNetV2 encoder + SA-MSDFM + CGFIM decoder modules)

title: FaceAge+: training-free synthetic augmentation for deep learning-based biological age estimation from facial images
task: Address age imbalance in facial age estimation via synthetic augmentation
key_results: MAE 3.27 years on UTKFace, 2.20 years on IMDb-Wiki; 25% error reduction for age 60+ cohort
comments: Training-free synthesis approach is elegant and practical; however, generalization to out-of-distribution populations (e.g., non-western ethnicities) not thoroughly assessed.

model_io.model: FaceAge+ (StyleGAN2 W-space traversal + DINOv3 feature extraction)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Synthetic age-conditioned face augmentation reduces prediction error in underrepresented age groups without end-to-end retraining
hypotheses.result: MAE improvements of 25% for elderly cohorts; effective across UTKFace and IMDb-Wiki

title: Decoupling of allele frequency and predicted pathogenicity in the tandem repeat filaggrin (FLG) gene
task: Map repeat-structure-dependent evolutionary constraint and population history in filaggrin (FLG) tandem repeats
key_results: FLG repeat architecture exhibits spatial discordance: predicted pathogenic variants enriched in terminal repeats; observed alleles concentrated in central-repeat truncations with strong ancestry correlation; common variants (AF>0.01) lack definitive pathogenic annotations
comments: Novel framework demonstrating that repeat structure and demographic history supersede uniform selection in variant interpretation; implications extend broadly to interpretation of copy-number and structure-variable regions.

model_io.model: Integration of population genetics (gnomAD, n>140,000) with AlphaMissense deep learning predictions

hypotheses.hypothesis: FLG repeat architecture and population history jointly determine variant distribution, superseding uniform selection
hypotheses.result: Pathogenic predictions enriched in terminal repeats; observed alleles concentrated in central repeats with strong ancestry alignment; demographic forces override uniform functional constraints

title: Prediction of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease using machine learning models
task: Predict chronic obstructive pulmonary disease risk using machine learning
key_results: Random forest achieved 83% accuracy, AUC-ROC=0.89, AUC-PR=0.78 on 42,941 individuals; key features: age, smoking history, comorbidities
comments: Large diverse cohort and accessible clinical feature set are strengths; competitive but not superior performance compared to studies with specialized data; external validation on different healthcare systems recommended.

model_io.model: Random forest (vs. multi-layer perceptron, support vector machine)
inputs: demographic, lifestyle, clinical features from All of Us database (42,941 individuals)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Machine learning models trained on accessible clinical features can achieve competitive COPD risk prediction for early intervention
hypotheses.result: Random forest AUC-ROC=0.89, accuracy=83%; age, smoking, comorbidities identified as key features

title: Dynamic feature pyramid network for real-time gesture recognition
task: Real-time gesture recognition for VR/AR
key_results: 84.88% accuracy with 20ms inference time on Tesla V100; faster convergence than baselines
comments: Strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off demonstrated, though evaluation limited to synthetic gesture datasets rather than deployed AR/VR systems.

model_io.model: Dynamic Feature Pyramid Network (DFPN)
inputs: hand images at variable angles and postures

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive dynamic convolutions with multi-scale feature fusion improve recognition under rotation and background variation
hypotheses.result: 84.88% accuracy achieved; superior gradient flow during training

title: Integrative analysis of network pharmacology and machine learning suggests potential anti-colorectal cancer mechanisms of Taohong-Siwu decoction
task: Identify anti-colorectal cancer mechanisms of Taohong-Siwu herbal decoction via network pharmacology and machine learning
key_results: Five core targets (CPT1A, CMA1, BCHE, CA7, CA1) downregulated in CRC; kaempferol strongly bound CA1 (MD-stable); in vitro: kaempferol suppressed HCT116 viability/migration, upregulated CA1; CA1 knockdown partially attenuated effects

model_io.model: Integrated network pharmacology + machine learning + molecular docking + MD simulation + experimental validation
inputs: GEO CRC expression data (GSE44076, GSE9348, GSE23878)
outputs: pathway enrichment (nitrogen metabolism, cell cycle, p53)

hypotheses.hypothesis: THSWD exerts anti-CRC effects via multi-component targeting of CPT1A/CMA1/BCHE/CA7/CA1 and modulation of metabolic/signaling pathways and immune microenvironment
hypotheses.result: Kaempferol (representative compound) suppressed HCT116 viability and migration; CA1 knockdown partially attenuated effects; core genes downregulated across three independent cohorts

title: DLGDFNet: a lung tumor image segmentation model based on local and global dual dynamic fusion
task: Lung tumor segmentation in CT images via local-global dual dynamic fusion
key_results: Effective performance on Lung-PET-CT-Dx, MSD, QIN-LungCT, LIDC-IDRI datasets; cross-dataset robustness demonstrated
comments: Framework integrates input-relevant local dynamic convolution with global attention; boundary preservation claims require quantitative validation against window-based attention baselines.

model_io.model: LGDFNet (Local-Global Dual Dynamic Fusion Network)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combining local dynamic convolution with global self-attention improves joint contextual and anatomical modeling
hypotheses.result: Cross-dataset robustness confirmed across four public datasets

title: Artificial intelligence-based photographic detection of pink esthetic score attributes using a hybrid deep learning segmentation pipeline: a method development study

comments: Transparent segmentation-based approach more interpretable than end-to-end prediction; moderate agreement on total PES suggests room for improvement in compound aesthetic judgments.

title: Metagenomic characterization of Acinetobacter in rivers reveals health-related risks, ecological functions, and underrepresented genomic diversity
task: Metagenomic characterization of Acinetobacter in river ecosystems and health implications
key_results: 1,253 river metagenomes analyzed; 202 metagenome-assembled genomes recovered from 38 species; 36 MAGs harbor resistance genes across 10 antibiotic, 22 biocide, 7 metal classes; genes for persistent organic pollutant degradation identified
comments: Comprehensive environmental genotyping; however, direct link between resistance dissemination and ecological functions remains correlative and warrants experimental validation.

model_io.model: Large-scale metagenomic analysis pipeline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Environmental Acinetobacter MAGs harbor both resistance and ecological functional genes, linking resistance dissemination to ecosystem processes
hypotheses.result: 36 of 38 recovered MAGs showed resistance-related and ecological functional genes; gaps in reference genomes confirmed

title: Hyperparameter-optimized deep learning for next-day pH forecasting in distributed water quality monitoring systems
task: Next-day pH forecasting in distributed water-quality monitoring via optimized regression models
key_results: OCOA-RegNet achieved RMSE 4.58×10⁻⁴±2.10×10⁻⁵; baseline RegNet RMSE 0.0285; metaheuristic hyperparameter optimization substantially improved performance
comments: Disciplined two-stage framework (baseline benchmarking + optimizer-guided refinement) demonstrates value of systematic hyperparameter tuning; spatio-temporal framing could benefit from explicit graph-based spatial modeling.

inputs: Water Quality Prediction dataset (Georgia, USA); multi-site, time-indexed pH and environmental measurements

hypotheses.result: OCOA-RegNet achieved lowest RMSE (4.58×10⁻⁴) with superior consistency across independent runs vs. eight alternative optimizers

title: High-accuracy lung region segmentation and injury classification using deep networks

four severity classes (No Lesion, Mild, Moderate, Severe)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Normalization is the dominant preprocessing contributor to classification performance

title: Quantifying vaccination thresholds and roll-out delays in an influenza transmission model with waning and immune boosting

model_io.model: SVIRLQS epidemiological model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Earlier and more aggressive vaccination deployment reduces transmission potential and outbreak burden in influenza dynamics with waning immunity

title: Reliable and calibrated diabetic retinopathy grading from Gaussian-filtered fundus images using attention and gated state-space feature mixing

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combining multi-scale feature pyramids, local attention, global state-space modeling, and calibration-aware loss improves accurate and reliable DR grading

title: Impact of temporal patterns in working contacts on epidemic spread
task: Model effects of temporal workplace contact heterogeneity on respiratory infection spread
key_results: Uniform daily contacts yield higher prevalence for short latent periods (1–2 days), lower for long latencies (5–6 days); effect diminishes with long infectious periods (≥7 days) but pronounced at lower R₀; weekday heterogeneity can substantially alter estimates
comments: Individual-based modeling with synthetic 5-million-person population reveals non-intuitive effects of temporal contact variation on reproduction number estimation; implications for policy-relevant parameterization of epidemic models.

model_io.model: GEMS (German Epidemic Micro-Simulation System) stochastic individual-based model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temporal heterogeneity in workplace contacts significantly affects infectious disease transmission dynamics and reproduction number estimation, especially for short latent periods and low R₀
hypotheses.result: Uniform contacts yield higher prevalence for short latencies (1–2 days); effect diminishes for long infectious periods (≥7 days) but remains pronounced at low R₀

title: Prognostic signatures associated with immune and macrophage phenotypes in colorectal cancer: integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses
task: Identify immune and macrophage phenotype signatures predicting colorectal cancer progression
key_results: Three-gene signature (FABP4/PPARGC1A/LEP) strongly prognostic; risk stratification associated with distinct immune profiles, pathway activities, mutations, drug sensitivity; single-cell analysis identified macrophages as central interacting cells

model_io.model: Integrative genomics pipeline (TCGA CRC bulk + single-cell RNA-seq)
inputs: bulk RNA-seq from CRC vs. normal
outputs: risk groups with distinct immune/pathway/mutation profiles

hypotheses.hypothesis: FABP4/PPARGC1A/LEP signature reflects macrophage-mediated immune suppression driving CRC progression
hypotheses.result: Risk stratification associated with M2 macrophage enrichment, immune suppression pathways; RT-qPCR validation confirmed downregulation in CRC

title: Inducing transcription in a gene desert is associated with locally increased replication activity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local transcriptional activation increases replication activity in a gene-poor late-replicating region independent of cassette orientation

title: Integrative multi-cohort bioinformatics and machine learning analysis reveals dysregulation of pro-inflammatory and pro-resolving lipid mediator pathway genes in atherosclerosis
